findings.title: Update decides login-cache invalidation using the org-aware model, which disagrees with what the cached list contains
findings.body:
In `update`, the 'original' IDP comes from `getById()` (line 91). That method returns `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...)`, whose `isEnabled()` returns false when the linked organization is disabled, or when organizations are disabled for the realm.

The cached login ID lists, however, are filled from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`. That is a raw DB query on the ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN/BROKER_PUBLIC columns and ignores organization status.

Example: an org is disabled and one of its public, enabled IDPs is in the cached list. An admin then sets that IDP to hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true, or removes BROKER_PUBLIC. `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` is false because the wrapped `isEnabled()` is false. `test(updated)` is also false. So `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` returns early (line 405) and nothing is invalidated.

The stale ID stays in the cached list. Once the org is re-enabled, `getForLogin` keeps returning it. `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` only re-checks `isEnabled()`, so a hidden, link-only, or non-public broker appears on the login page until some other change invalidates the cache.

Fix: evaluate the original with the raw model (e.g. `idpDelegate.getById(...)`), so the comparison uses the same view as the cached query.

findings.title: Merging a previously read query can re-insert stale search results after a concurrent invalidation
findings.body:
When the cached `IdentityProviderListQuery` exists but lacks the current `searchKey`, the code proceeds in this order:
1. It reads `query` (line 222).
2. It calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`.
3. It reads a fresh revision.
4. It builds a new query that copies all of the old query's searches (`new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)`).
5. It adds the result with `cache.getCurrentCounter()`.

If another transaction invalidates `cacheKey` between steps 1 and 2, the old searches are already stale. They still get merged in and stored with an up-to-date revision, so `addRevisioned` accepts them. Typical triggers are creating, removing, or relinking a login IDP.

The login cache can then keep serving outdated ID lists for other organizations: newly added brokers go missing, or brokers that became hidden or unlinked still show. This copies the pattern from `getByOrganization`, but it now affects the login page. The merge should be dropped, or the code should verify the entry was not invalidated between the read and the re-add.

findings.title: Single cache entry per fetch mode accumulates one result set per organization and is rebuilt on every new org
findings.body:
The cache key is only realm + FetchMode, and the organization ID is used as a search key inside one `IdentityProviderListQuery`. For `ALL`/`ORG_ONLY` with an organizationId, each organization not yet seen does three things:
- triggers `invalidateObject` on the shared entry,
- copies the entire existing map of searches,
- re-adds it.

In realms with many organizations, this entry grows without bound, since it holds a set per org. It is also repeatedly invalidated and copied during normal login traffic. Any login-relevant IDP change then discards all of it at once. Consider keying the cache entry by organization (as `getByOrganization` does with `cacheKeyOrgId`), or bounding the stored searches.

findings.title: Test cleanup removes IDP with literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDPs
findings.body:
`getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` points at an IDP named "alias", which does not exist. The same mistake appears again at line 425. None of the 21 IDPs created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` (`idp-alias-0`..`idp-alias-20`) are ever cleaned up.

If the realm is not re-imported, they leak into other tests. Re-running the test would also make the `create(...)` calls fail with conflicts that go unnoticed, because the responses are closed without checking status. The cleanup should use the real alias (e.g. `get("idp-alias-" + i)`).
